rule: Groups are taken in this fixed order. A group is kept whole or dropped whole, so a comparison is never split across the cap. Network execution is deduplicated and experimental relationships are not: a comparison that has an arm identical to an already selected network reuses it and adds only its distinct counterpart, a comparison whose arms are all selected costs nothing and is kept, and the record lists what each group deployed and reused. The cap of 10 counts distinct network_content_sha256 identities (the E-3 anchor included, the reading of the #327 stage 1 budget 'about 10 nets and the E-3 anchor' that keeps the total at 10). A group that would exceed the cap is skipped whole and the next one considered. No measured quality of any network is an input.
priority: Evidence-driven, not chronological. Tier A: the reference (E-3 is the only net that has played) and the base recipe. Tier B: one representative of each distinct training signal, because nets that share a recipe are expected to land in the same place on a 60 game screen that only drops nets below 0.10. Tier C: replicates of an already represented recipe, which give the spread needed to read any difference between recipes: M-1 seeds 43 and 44 are pure seed replicates of the base recipe, and P3A-001 differs from it by 75 sentinel rows with a held-out figure (+0.0002) inside the M-1 seed spread (0.5898 to 0.5977), so it is no more informative than a seed replicate and precedes none of them. Tier D: later checkpoints and further seeds of recipes already represented.
